items.desc: A top-five NHL Draft pick in 2022, Shane Wright subsequently struggled to find his footing in Seattle.

items.title: Predators acquire Shane Wright from Kraken for Matthew Wood
items.desc: The Predators and Kraken swap former first-round picks as Wright finally finds a change of scenery.

items.title: Predators acquire Shane Wright from Kraken for Matthew Wood
items.desc: The Nashville Predators traded forward Matthew Wood to the Seattle Kraken for forward Shane Wright on Sunday.

stories.take:
The Athletic reports that Seattle has traded Shane Wright to Nashville for Matthew Wood, and Daily Faceoff describes it as a swap of former first-round picks that gives Wright a change of scenery. Wright went fourth overall in 2022, and Wood went 15th in 2023.

The numbers say this is a swap of two similar, slumping players. So far this season, Wright has 3 goals in 14 games against 3.74 expected goals (the number of goals a player's shot quality would typically produce), a shortfall of 0.74. Wood has 1 goal against 3.12 expected, a gap of 2.12. In that sense Wood has been the unluckier finisher, and his scoring should drift up if his chances keep coming. Both sit below even at five-on-five, with Wright at 47 percent of expected goals and Wood at 47 percent, and both play about 14 minutes a night. Seattle is 8-5-1 despite a 44.9 percent expected goal share, helped by 10.7 more goals than expected. We'd read that as a team outperforming its chances, so the Kraken's record is sturdier than their process. Nashville is 5-4-5 with a 48.9 share, a bit better than its results. Neither player moves the needle much on his own, but Wright gets a new look in Nashville.

stories.title: Capitals place Dylan McIlrath on waivers
stories.desc: McIlrath was a healthy scratch for eight of the Capitals’ 12 games before the waiver placement.

items.title: Capitals place Dylan McIlrath on waivers
items.desc: McIlrath was a healthy scratch for eight of the Capitals’ 12 games before the waiver placement.

stories.take:
Daily Faceoff reports the Capitals have placed Dylan McIlrath on waivers, noting he was a healthy scratch for eight of Washington's 12 games before the move. NHL.com's Tom Gulitti posted that coach Spencer Carbery said the move opens the roster spot for Remi Poirier.

Our numbers show why this is a small loss on the ice. In four games so far this season, McIlrath averaged 6.58 minutes with no points. The team's share of expected goals (a measure of chance quality) was 51.45 percent at five-on-five while he played, but Washington's overall share of chances ran 1.46 points better with him off the ice. The sample is tiny, so we wouldn't read much into it, but nothing suggests the Capitals lose something real. They are 8-5-0 with a 53 percent five-on-five expected goal share, and their goaltending has saved 2.9 goals more than expected, which is propping up the record more than the scoring has. Losing a depth defenseman who barely played shouldn't change that picture.

stories.title: Lightning GM Julien BriseBois Draws Another Hard Line With Nikita Kucherov Contract Negotiations
stories.desc: The Tampa Bay Lightning have enjoyed great success recently, but Bolts GM Julien BriseBois is showing he won't just hand his team's icons a blank check on their next contract. Tampa moved on from Steven Stamkos, and now they're doing so with Nikita Kucherov.…

items.title: Lightning GM Julien BriseBois Draws Another Hard Line With Nikita Kucherov Contract Negotiations
items.desc: The Tampa Bay Lightning have enjoyed great success recently, but Bolts GM Julien BriseBois is showing he won't just hand his team's icons a blank check on their next contract. Tampa moved on from Steven Stamkos, and now they're doing so with Nikita Kucherov.…

stories.take:
The Hockey News reports that Lightning GM Julien BriseBois is drawing another hard line in contract talks, this time with Nikita Kucherov, after Tampa Bay moved on from Steven Stamkos. As Daily Faceoff's Leafs coverage posted, Elliotte Friedman reports Toronto is among the teams Kucherov would consider being traded to.

On the ice, Kucherov looks every bit the player worth the fight. He has 18 points in 13 games so far this season, and his goals (4) sit almost exactly on his expected goals (4.18), which measures the quality of his chances. So the production is real, not a hot streak. When he plays at 5-on-5, TBL controls about 59% of the expected goals, and the team's share is about six points better with him out there. That matters because TBL's goaltending has been a problem: the team is 4 goals saved above expected in the red. The skaters are carrying it, and Kucherov leads them.

Stamkos is a useful contrast. His 8 goals beat his expected 5.53 by nearly two and a half, and NSH's 5-on-5 share is lower with him on the ice. We'd call his start more fortunate than dominant.

items.title: Flyers activate Travis Konecny, Owen Tippett off injured reserve
items.desc: Konecny has missed Philadelphia’s last 10 games, while Tippett has missed the last six games.

stories.take:
Daily Faceoff reports the Flyers have activated Travis Konecny and Owen Tippett off injured reserve, with Konecny having missed 10 games and Tippett six. As Charlie O'Connor of PHLY Sports posted, "As expected, Tippett and Konecny are on the ice for warmups. They're back today."

Philadelphia (3-8-4) could use the help, since our numbers have the team getting 42 percent of the expected goals, a measure of chance quality, so far this season. Konecny has no goals in five games, but his own expected goals are 0.98, so the shots he gets are decent and the finishing has lagged. Last season he scored 27 goals in 77 games, which suggests the goals should come. Tippett looks shakier. He has one goal in nine games, and the Flyers get only 32 percent of the 5-on-5 expected goals when he's on the ice, with the team's share 9 points worse with him out there than without him so far this season. Konecny's return looks like the more useful one for the lineup, while Tippett needs to show a better two-way game.

stories.title: Islanders’ Ryan Pulock out 2-4 weeks with upper-body injury
stories.desc: Pulock suffered the injury during Thursday’s 4-3 overtime win against the Minnesota Wild.

items.title: Islanders’ Ryan Pulock out 2-4 weeks with upper-body injury
items.desc: Pulock suffered the injury during Thursday’s 4-3 overtime win against the Minnesota Wild.

stories.take:
Daily Faceoff reports that Islanders defenseman Ryan Pulock is out two to four weeks with an upper-body injury, suffered in Thursday's 4-3 overtime win over the Minnesota Wild. NHL.com's Stefen Rosner posted that the Islanders sending Isaiah Georget back to Hamilton could mean positive news, though he stressed he didn't want to assume.

Pulock's numbers so far this season are not those of a player the Islanders can't spare. In 13 games he has one assist, and his 42% share of the 5-on-5 chances (expected goals, the quality of shots each side gets) is the kind of number you'd rather not see from a 17:51 regular. NYI also does better without that pair on the ice, by 12 percentage points of chance share. Last season, by contrast, he had 27 points in 76 games, so this looks like a rough start rather than a new level. The Islanders sit at 46% of expected goals overall and lean on goaltending, 10 goals saved above expected, so losing a defenseman matters more than his stats suggest. In the one game since he went out, Matthew Schaefer has moved in beside Pelech and Tony DeAngelo is up to 20:51 a night from 17:13. That is one game, so treat it as a first read.

stories.title: Bruins’ Nikita Zadorov fined for roughing Blackhawks’ Alex Vlasic
stories.desc: The Bruins defeated the Blackhawks 5-4 in OT on Saturday.

items.title: Bruins’ Nikita Zadorov fined for roughing Blackhawks’ Alex Vlasic
items.desc: The Bruins defeated the Blackhawks 5-4 in OT on Saturday.

stories.take:
Daily Faceoff reports that Bruins defenseman Nikita Zadorov was fined for roughing Blackhawks defenseman Alex Vlasic, after Boston beat Chicago 5-4 in overtime on Saturday. As The Athletic's Scott Powers posted, "Vlasic and Mittelstadt get two minutes for roughing. Zadorov gets a 10-minute misconduct."

The fine matters less than what the two teams' numbers show. Boston is 10-4-1, but the record flatters them a little: they've drawn about even in chance quality, with a 50.5 percent share of expected goals (a measure of how good the shots each side gets). Goalies have done the lifting, saving 11.5 goals more than expected so far this season. Chicago, 4-9-1, has been outplayed (43.2 percent) and is 8 goals short of what its chances should have produced, so some of that record is bad finishing luck. As for the two defensemen, both are pointless in goals through 14 games, and both have been slightly worse for their teams with them on the ice, by about two and a half points of expected goal share. Vlasic's 39 percent at five-on-five is the bigger concern, and he plays 20.5 minutes a night.

items.title: Red Wings' Dylan Larkin Reportedly Could Alter His NHL Trade List
items.desc: Dylan Larkin has played his final game with the Detroit Red Wings as he awaits a trade. In his pursuit of a trade, NHL insider Elliotte Friedman reported that Larkin could alter his list of destinations.

stories.take:
The Hockey News argues that interim GM Shawn Horcoff made a strong case for the full-time job with how he handled his press conference on Thursday, as he works to trade Dylan Larkin, the disgruntled ex-captain. The Detroit Red Wings have been without a full-time GM since mid-July.

Larkin's results undersell his play so far this season. He has 2 goals in 10 games, but his own expected goals (a measure of the quality of his chances) come to 3.03, so he is about one goal short of what those chances should have produced. Detroit controls 56.3% of the expected goals at 5-on-5 when he plays, and the team's share improves by 1.53 percentage points with him on the ice. Last season he scored 34 goals and 67 points in 74 games. For a buyer, that points to a player whose scoring should recover, though ten games is a small sample. As for Detroit, its 53.3% share of expected goals is solid, but it sits 7.2 goals below expected, which is part of why the record is a modest 6-5-3. Moving Larkin would remove a top-line forward who is still driving play.

items.title: Lightning’s Cooper says Kucherov still fully committed to team despite trade request
items.desc: Cooper spoke to the media ahead of Tampa Bay’s game against the Nashville Predators on Saturday.

stories.take:
The Athletic reports that Nikita Kucherov has told the Lightning he won't re-sign and has asked for a trade; Daily Faceoff carries the same report. The Athletic notes he is set to become an unrestricted free agent after this season.

What a team would be getting is a player still producing at the top of the league. Kucherov has four goals and 15 points in 12 games so far this season, and his results match his chances: his own expected goals (the quality of his shots) are 3.98 against four goals scored, so nothing here is luck. At five-on-five, Tampa Bay generates 57.61% of the expected goals while he is on the ice, and the team's share of the expected goals is 2.11 percentage points better with him out there. His 20.75 minutes a game and last season's 44 goals and 130 points fit the same picture.

For Tampa Bay, the timing matters. At 8-3-1, the Lightning control 56.9% of the expected goals as a team, so this is a contender deciding whether to move its best player. For fantasy managers, the trade ask adds uncertainty about where he lands, but the underlying numbers give no reason to doubt his output.

items.title: Islanders’ Emil Heineman ejected after hit on Oilers’ Isaac Howard
items.desc: No update on Howard’s condition was available at the end of the first period after suffering the knee-on-knee hit.

stories.take:
Islanders forward Emil Heineman was ejected early in Saturday's game against the Oilers for a knee-on-knee hit that injured Edmonton wing Isaac Howard, per ESPN. Daily Faceoff adds that no update on Howard's condition was available at the end of the first period.

Howard is a depth piece for Edmonton so far this season. He averages 9.59 minutes a game, and the Oilers have controlled a smaller share of the quality chances at five-on-five with him on the ice (about 38 percent of expected goals, a measure of shot quality) than without him. His one goal is right in line with the chances he's produced, so there's no hidden scoring luck to lose. Edmonton can absorb the absence. For the Islanders, Heineman is a 15.87-minute forward whose team has done slightly better with him on the ice, so a suspension would cost New York real depth. Going by how the coach has used his players, Victor Eklund, at 14:08 a night, is next in line for those minutes.

stories.title: Ducks place Nick Jensen on waivers
stories.desc: Jensen signed a two-year, $2.25 million AAV contract with the Ducks on July 1.

items.title: Ducks place Nick Jensen on waivers
items.desc: Jensen signed a two-year, $2.25 million AAV contract with the Ducks on July 1.

stories.take:
Daily Faceoff reports that the Ducks have placed defenseman Nick Jensen on waivers, noting he signed a two-year deal worth $2.25 million per season with Anaheim on July 1. That is a quick turnaround for a signing less than four months old.

Our numbers help explain it. Jensen has played only three games for ANA so far this season, scoring one goal and adding one assist, but his goal came from a shot quality that should have produced about 0.21 expected goals (the measure of how good a player's own chances were), so he is running well ahead of his shooting. At five-on-five, Anaheim has generated just 31 percent of the expected goals while he is on the ice, and the team's share is about 15 percentage points better with him off it. For a team sitting at 5-7-1 with a 44 percent five-on-five expected goal share, that is the wrong direction. Anaheim has bigger problems than one depth defenseman, but our data suggests this waiver move is about on-ice results, not a fluke of small sample size.

stories.title: Blues’ Colton Parayko day-to-day with upper-body injury
stories.desc: The Blues recalled Theo Lindstein to take Parayko’s place for Saturday’s game in Detroit.

items.title: Blues’ Colton Parayko day-to-day with upper-body injury
items.desc: The Blues recalled Theo Lindstein to take Parayko’s place for Saturday’s game in Detroit.

stories.take:
Daily Faceoff reports that Blues defenseman Colton Parayko is day-to-day with an upper-body injury, and St. Louis recalled Theo Lindstein to take his place for Saturday's game in Detroit.

Parayko has been asked to carry heavy minutes, 20.81 a night, and so far this season he has no goals and four assists in 13 games. His own chances have been modest: 1.26 expected goals (a measure of shot quality), against zero actual goals. At 5-on-5 the Blues have generated 47.69 percent of the expected goals with him on the ice, and the team does better without him by 3.88 points. That is a small sample, but it suggests his results are not hiding a much stronger player. Lindstein, in four games, sits at 38.73 percent, so the drop-off is real if he draws extra minutes. Going by how the coach has used his players, Cam Fowler, at 20:57 a night, is next in line for Parayko's minutes. Watch whether St. Louis leans on Fowler more, since the Blues are 6-6-1 and holding close to even at 50.3 percent of expected goals overall.

items.title: Leafs activate Chris Tanev from injured reserve
items.desc: Tanev has missed over three weeks due to an upper-body injury, but is expected to return to the lineup on Saturday night.

stories.take:
Daily Faceoff reports that Toronto has activated defenseman Chris Tanev from injured reserve. He missed more than three weeks with an upper-body injury and is expected back in the lineup Saturday night. The Leafs Nation, via Daily Faceoff Toronto, posted that he's been paired with Morgan Rielly in practice.

Tanev's numbers so far this season are a small sample, six games, but they aren't flattering. He has no goals and one assist, and the Leafs have controlled just 41 percent of the 5-on-5 expected goals (a measure of chance quality) with him on the ice. Toronto's share improves by about five points when he sits, so he hasn't yet helped the team win the shot-quality battle. That matters because the Leafs are 7-6-2 and sit at 47 percent of expected goals overall, with a plus-9.8 gap between goals scored and expected, which suggests their results are running ahead of their play. Tanev's role is a defensive one, and he averages almost 17 minutes a night, so a quick return to form would help the penalty kill, which allows 0.75 expected goals per game. Fantasy managers shouldn't expect much offense from him.

items.title: Canadiens’ Mike Matheson out two weeks with lower-body injury
items.desc: Matheson missed four games earlier this season with a lower-body injury.

stories.take:
Daily Faceoff reports that Montreal defenseman Mike Matheson will be out two weeks with a lower-body injury, and notes he already missed four games earlier this season with one. Karine Hains of The Hockey News posted the same news alongside word that Montembeault is day to day.

Matheson matters to a team playing well. MTL is 8-3-2 and controls 54 percent of the quality chances (expected goals) at five-on-five, though the Habs have leaned on goaltending, with 5.6 goals saved above expected so far this season. Matheson logs 23.76 minutes a night and has four points in eight games, but his own numbers are ordinary: the team's share of chances is 2.2 points worse with him on the ice, and his 51.34 percent five-on-five share is only slightly better than even. His absence shouldn't swing the club much. In the one game since he went out, Kaiden Guhle moved up from 21:15 to 25:02 a night, and Alexandre Carrier from 20:19 to 23:47. That is a single game, so treat it as a first read on how the coach is deploying them. Guhle and Carrier are the defensemen to roster while Matheson sits.

items.title: The airline lost my (hockey) bag: Inside an NHL player's delayed season debut

stories.take:
The Athletic reports that Dakota Joshua's season debut with the Maple Leafs was delayed after an airline lost his hockey bag, which the outlet says was far more than a minor inconvenience for him.

The bigger question for Toronto is what the team around him looks like. TOR sits at 7-6-2 with 16 points through 15 games, but our numbers see a team playing worse than that record. Its share of expected goals, which measures the quality of chances for and against, is 47%, and it drops to 45% at five-on-five, so the Leafs are being outchanced in most of their even-strength minutes. They have scored 9.8 more goals than their chances would predict, and goalies have stopped 2.2 more than expected, so finishing and goaltending are both helping. Special teams are fine: the power play generates 0.71 expected goals per game and the penalty kill allows 0.75. The record is outrunning the underlying play so far this season, and a new forward alone won't close that gap.

items.title: Senators’ Hodgson suspended for boarding Kings’ Clarke
items.desc: Hodgson has no suspension history in the NHL, but was fined for boarding during the 2025 preseason.

stories.take:
ESPN reports that Ottawa forward Hayden Hodgson was suspended two games by the NHL's Department of Player Safety for charging and boarding Los Angeles defenseman Brandt Clarke. The Athletic notes he drew a five-minute major and a game misconduct on the play, and Daily Faceoff adds he has no suspension history but was fined for boarding in the 2025 preseason.

For Ottawa, the loss is small. Hodgson, who was never drafted and came up as a free agent via the ECHL, has played about 5.1 minutes a game and has no points in five games so far this season. His 5-on-5 expected goal share (the share of scoring chances, weighted by quality, that his team gets while he's on the ice) is 41 percent, and the Senators' share improves by 9.2 points when he sits. The Senators (8-5-1) sit at 50 percent at 5-on-5, so this barely dents them. It matters more for Los Angeles. Clarke has been a real driver so far this season: a 56 percent share at 5-on-5, a 15-point team swing when he plays, and nine points in 12 games for a 4-6-2 club that needs him in the lineup.

As EP Rinkside's Sean Shapiro posted, "Dylan Larkin won't play tonight. Todd McLellan says Shawn Horcoff will address that situation."

If he goes, Detroit loses a player whose results trail his chances. Larkin has two goals in 10 games so far this season against about three expected goals (the number a player should score given the quality of his shots), a gap of about one goal. His 21.69 minutes a game are heavy, and at 5-on-5 the Red Wings generate 56.3% of the expected goals with him on the ice. The team's share of the shot quality is about 2.6 percentage points better when he plays. DET sits at 5-4-3 with 13 points and a 52.3% share of expected goals, so the underlying game is decent, but the team is 8 goals below expected. Losing a 34-goal scorer from last season won't help that. For fantasy, his value depends on where he lands, and a goal total running behind his chances argues for patience.

stories.title: The Hockey News Morning Skate: Bobrovsky Struggles In Seattle, Cooley Injured As Oilers Beat Flames
stories.desc: In this edition of The Hockey News Morning Skate, Eric Cruikshank and Michael Traikos break down Devin Cooley's injury in the Edmonton Oilers' win over the Calgary Flames, Sergei Bobrovsky's struggles against the Seattle Kraken, and more.

items.title: The Hockey News Morning Skate: Bobrovsky Struggles In Seattle, Cooley Injured As Oilers Beat Flames
items.desc: In this edition of The Hockey News Morning Skate, Eric Cruikshank and Michael Traikos break down Devin Cooley's injury in the Edmonton Oilers' win over the Calgary Flames, Sergei Bobrovsky's struggles against the Seattle Kraken, and more.

stories.take:
The Hockey News' Morning Skate reports that Calgary goalie Devin Cooley was injured in the Oilers' win over the Flames, and that Sergei Bobrovsky struggled against Seattle. The write-up doesn't say how serious Cooley's injury is.

If he's out, it hurts. Cooley has been a bright spot in a rough start for CGY. His goals saved above expected (how many goals a goalie stops compared with an average goalie facing the same shots) is +2.19 in seven games so far this season, on top of a .912 save percentage. Last year he was +17.23 over 31 games. As a team, Calgary sits at -5.5 in that measure and is 5-7-0, so the goaltending has not been the problem when he plays. Without him, that picture could change quickly.

Bobrovsky's .885 save percentage looks ugly, but his goals saved above expected is +0.92 in 10 games, so he has been a bit better than the shots he's faced. That's a far cry from last season's -13.5 over 52 games. We'd call this a slow start with some luck-adjusted support, not proof the decline is over.

items.title: Pressure Is Mounting For Oilers' Jake Walman As Early Defensive Struggles Lead To Healthy Scratch
items.desc: It's been a tough start for to the season for Edmonton Oilers defenseman Jake Walman, and head coach Mike Babcock made the 30-year-old a healthy scratch against the Calgary Flames. What's gone wrong and what needs to change?

stories.take:
The Hockey News reports that Oilers defenseman Jake Walman was a healthy scratch against the Calgary Flames after a rough start to the season, with the piece asking what has gone wrong and what needs to change.

The numbers back up the concern, though not in a dramatic way. So far this season Walman has one assist in nine games and no goals, and his own expected goals (a measure of the quality of the chances he generates) sit at 0.52, so he is about half a goal behind where those chances say he should be. That points to some bad finishing luck, but the larger issue is how the team fares with him on the ice. At five-on-five, Edmonton gets 46 percent of the expected goals when he plays, and the team's share is 2.5 percentage points better when he isn't out there. He is also 30 and had 20 points in 53 games last year, so there is no big offensive history to lean on. For fantasy, he is a drop in most formats. For Edmonton, the scratch looks like a coaching response to measurable defensive slippage, not an overreaction.
